transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Li (Redwood), Priya Nair (HelioFin Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (HelioFin Platform), Lena Vogel (HelioFin Security), Aaron Brooks (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Redwood and HelioFin reviewed POC model compatibility matrix, compared quantization tradeoffs and pinned versions for canary. Discussed rollback runbook and guardrails (routing fallbacks, metrics to watch). Security questions on logs/KMS were flagged. Next steps are sharing a matrix, runbook draft, HelioFin to run targeted benchmarks and schedule a dry-run.

Topics: catalog compatibility, model pinning strategy, soft vs hard fallback, canary/rollback playbook, telemetry and SLI thresholds, security/logging requirements

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: alright hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off, I see Priya, Tom, Lena, Aaron thanks for making time, we wanted to focus on the compat matrix and an actual rollback runbook so you can dry run this with your SREs
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, Maya. quick context, we ran the q3 branch comparisons you sent, we saw decent latencies but the output distribution changed a little on long form accountant reports, so this is why pinning and rollbacks matter for us
[00:37] Daniel: yah and to be clear when you say "distribution changed" do you mean token probs or formatting shifts?
[00:42] Priya: formatting shifts — sometimes the bulleting comes out different and that cascades into our downstream parsers, so we need a safe fallback that doesn't blow up the pipeline
[00:52] Tom: for platform side we also care about the p95 under burst traffic, not just med. our p95 token length is like 820 tokens in peaks, so the runtime selection matters
[01:06] Maya: perfect noted. ok quick recap of what we updated in the compatibility matrix (link: https://redwood.example/compat/heliofin) — we added per-model rows showing quantization profile recommended, sequence length tested, memory envelope, and compatible runtime (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
[01:26] Noah: and we flagged models with known attention-kernel regressions on older GPUs — those are marked red in the sheet, those would require software patching or a change to a variant build
[01:37] Priya: can you clarify what you mean by "variant build"? is that the smaller param checkpoint or a half-precision config?
[01:44] Daniel: variant could be either — e.g., same checkpoint but different quantization (8bit-ptq vs 4bit-qat) or a different distilled model in the catalog. The key is compatibility: same API contract and similar logits behavior within our eval thresholds
[01:58] Lena: on security, we need to make sure rollback doesn't leak intermediate KV cache data to logs. can you confirm logs redact KV cache and prompt shards?
[02:08] Daniel: yep the platform doesn't log raw KV by default, but we will compile the runbook section that explicitly states what is and isn't captured. there was one past transcript where K V cash was incorrectly logged, so we will double-check
[02:24] Aaron: i ran a quick smoke yesterday, on the quantized variant we saw a 12% inference cost drop but p95 increased by ~90ms in the burst. that's in line with what you sent in the sheet
[02:36] Maya: cool. ok let's talk rollback runbook — high level we propose a three-stage plan: 1) detect via metric thresholds and canary health checks, 2) execute soft fallback (route subset of traffic to stable variant), 3) full rollback if soft fallback doesn't recover SLA within x minutes
[02:55] Priya: what do you suggest for metric thresholds? our NFRs are pretty strict: 99.9% availability and p95 under 700ms for interactive flows
[03:06] Daniel: recommended thresholds for this POC: error-rate jump >0.5% absolute OR degradation p95 increase >20% sustained for 5 minutes triggers canary shielding; if canary shielding fails within 10 minutes, escalate to full rollback. these numbers are tunable
[03:23] Tom: how does routing work for the soft fallback? is it by API key, route, or request header? we can't change all clients at once
[03:31] Noah: we support multiple routing policies — easiest for you would be route-level pinning: create a canary route that sends 10% of traffic to variant A and the rest to baseline; then bump to 50/50 during dry runs. we can also do header-based for specific customers
[03:45] Priya: ok that sounds workable, but we need determinism for audit. do you keep an immutable audit trail of route changes and rollbacks?
[03:53] Maya: yes, Console audit trails record change events, user, timestamp, and the diff. we'll include console screenshots in the runbook draft
[04:03] Lena: plus we need to ensure KMS access is limited during rollback automation — who executes the automatic rollback? a service account? human-in-the-loop?
[04:12] Daniel: default is human-ack for full rollback; soft fallback can be automated with a service principal that has scoped privileges. we'll show both patterns in the runbook with examples of IAM policies
[04:24] Aaron: quick note on canary traffic — we need sticky sessions for certain customers; the routing should honor the customer token so we don't split their session mid-stream
[04:34] Daniel: current routing honors session-token binding when you enable sticky mode, yep
[04:39] Maya: moving on to compatibility: Priya, you had asked about model pinning vs model gating — let's cover a few scenarios we recommended in the matrix
[04:49] Priya: yes, we want to pin for reporting pipelines but be more flexible for exploratory assistants. i.e., pin model versions for nightly batch reporting, allow shadowing for interactive features
[04:59] Daniel: exactly — so in the matrix we mark "pin=required" for batch jobs with schema bindings, and "pin=optional" for chat flows. we also recommended feature flags to flip pins per environment (staging -> prod)
[05:12] Tom: can you walk through an example rollback timeline? if we detect formatting regressions at 11:05, what's the expected timeline to get back to baseline?
[05:20] Noah: detection at t=0, soft fallback within 1-2 minutes routing 20% away, monitor for 5-10 mins; if indicators still bad, full rollback within 15 minutes assuming human-ack. target RTO we propose is 15-30 minutes depending on approval chain
[05:33] Priya: good. on the topic of evaluation thresholds, we shared our golden prompt set (link in chat). did you run that across the q4 and q3 variants?
[05:43] Daniel: yes we ran the golden set; for q4 quantized we saw 1.8% regression on strict parsing metrics, but for lenient metrics it was within noise. we'll attach the full eval CSV to the compatibility sheet
[05:57] Priya: that's helpful. is there an easy way to convert those diffs into alerting rules? we want to avoid manual checks
[06:05] Daniel: yes, the Console supports evaluating eval-run diffs; you can wire an alert when a metric drops below threshold; we'll include recommended alert rules in the runbook
[06:16] Tom: we also need to understand the cost delta if we keep soft fallback routes for longer — curious about unit economics when 30% of traffic stays on older larger model
[06:27] Maya: we added a cost column in the sheet showing per 1M tokens the delta between baseline and quantized variant; we can model mixed routing cost as weighted avg — we can run a scenario for your avg daily tokens after you share token counts
[06:40] Aaron: i'll share daily token counts and traffic distribution off-line
[06:43] Priya: ok another question, when you do full rollback does the KV cache get cleared or do you rely on cache compatibility? we've seen stale caches cause mismatched completions before
[06:52] Daniel: good point — the runbook calls out two strategies: 1) conservative: clear KV caches for affected shards (short downtime), 2) aggressive: allow cache compatibility if model variant is binary-compatible. we recommend conservative for first rollbacks and move to compatibility once validated
[07:08] Lena: from security perspective we need the exact s3 path for audit logs during rollback and retention policy on those logs
[07:14] Maya: we'll add those details. retention is configurable; default is 90 days for the POC but we can adjust per enterprise agreement
[07:22] Tom: do you have a sample playbook we can run as a tabletop exercise with our on-call?
[07:28] Daniel: yes Daniel: i'll attach a draft runbook with command snippets, and a dry-run checklist. we want to do the tabletop with you and your SREs; propose week of July 7th
[07:40] Priya: week of July 7th works for us, we need to sync on who will be primary and secondary responders
[07:46] Maya: great. switching gears — compatibility regressions sometimes only show at scale; what telemetry do you recommend for early warning?
[07:55] Noah: short list: per-route p95, perplexity drift on golden prompts, parse-fail rate from downstream parsers, token-efficiency (tokens per resolved entity), and error-rate by model version
[08:08] Priya: we'll add parse-fail rate, that was a big pain point
[08:12] Aaron: also want to track queuing time per request during bursts — that was the signal we missed last time
[08:17] Daniel: add queue-time histogram to the dashboards, we'll provide dashboard templates in the runbook
[08:22] Tom: question on canary sizing — you recommended 10% initially. is that random or thinned by user cohort? we need to exclude high-value clients from experiments by policy
[08:31] Maya: you can exclude by tag. we recommend targeting internal users and a small external cohort that signed up to early access. we will not include enterprise clients unless you opt-in
[08:42] Priya: perfect. on the topic of pin expiry — how do you prevent old pins from lingering in prod after a feature sunset?
[08:50] Daniel: runbook includes expiring pins with TTL and automated reminders; Console shows pinned routes with creation date and expiry meta so you can sweep stale pins
[08:58] Priya: useful. one more: rollback vs degrade — sometimes we just want to scale down model size rather than rollback to older checkpoint. does Redwood support dynamic model scaling?
[09:10] Noah: we support model families that are lighter weight; you can do a blue-green to a distilled variant as a degrade path. it's effectively a variant swap but we call it scale-down in the sheet
[09:22] Tom: ok let's talk about the dry-run. what environment should we use? staging or a production shadow route?
[09:27] Daniel: ideally both. do initial dry-run in staging with full traffic replay, then do a production shadow for a small percent of non-critical traffic. we'll document the exact steps
[09:36] Aaron: any gotchas around tokenization differences between variants? we saw minor token count diffs which change billing unexpectedly
[09:44] Maya: Right — tokenization drift is in the matrix as a risk. we recommend including token-delta checks in cost alerts so unexpected bill changes alert ops
[09:53] Priya: okay excellent. on timeline — to recap, you will share updated matrix by Thu (6/26) and runbook by Mon (6/30). heliofin will run benchmarks and share metrics by July 2nd. we will schedule tabletop week of July 7th. anyone disagree?
[10:08] Tom: sounds good
[10:10] Lena: no objections
[10:12] Maya: great. quick open questions from the team?
[10:16] Priya: can Redwood run a targeted eval that emphasizes nested-list formatting? it's where we saw most failures
[10:22] Daniel: yes we will run a focused eval set and include that in the eval CSV
[10:26] Aaron: small nit — can you include sample curl commands for sticky routing and for forcing a variant? ops would appreciate concrete steps in the runbook
[10:32] Noah: will do, sample commands included
[10:36] Priya: also please include the fallback metrics we'd use to flip the feature flag to prevent noisy alerts (i.e., guard windows)
[10:43] Daniel: guard windows included, default 5 min sliding window, with a 1-minute cooldown to avoid flapping
[10:48] Maya: excellent. i'll send the notes and links after this call. thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. we'll follow up with matrix + runbook drafts
[10:58] Priya: thanks all
[11:02] Tom: thanks
[11:05] Lena: bye
[41:23] (end of recording)
